title: The Sheinbaum-López Obrador Rupture
author: Álvaro Delgado Gómez
content:
_This article by[Álvaro Delgado
Gómez](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/delgado/) originally appeared in the
[September 1, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4863028/la-ruptura-sheinbaum-lopez-
obrador), an independent Mexican digital news outlet._

When Claudia Sheinbaum assumed the Presidency of the Republic, she was advised
to distance herself from Andrés Manuel López Obrador, to "move to the center,"
while at the same time they accused her of submitting to her predecessor, and
over time they invented a rift between the two that, in these days of Rubén
Rocha Moya's fleeting return and Andrés López Beltrán's visa, was presented as
a breakup, a fantasy that—once again—has had misogyny and authoritarian
nostalgia as its correlate.

The authors of such treacheries come from the rancid PRIAN conservatism and,
more specifically, from the addicts of Carlos Salinas de Gortari, the same
ones who dominate Mexico's information spaces and who were empowered during
the six-year term of this figure marked by electoral fraud, high corruption
and political repression, including disappearance and murder.

Just because Salinas de Gortari left the Presidency he stole in 1988 does not
mean that he has stopped having power and influence, which he exercises in the
economic, political, academic and intellectual spheres, and increasingly with
less effectiveness through his media and opinion-makers, who view the national
reality with the old categories of analysis, the PRI school of verticalism,
exacerbated presidentialism and serious corruption, not trifles.

It is these specimens of salinismo, and their apprentices, who invoke a
rupture between Sheinbaum and López Obrador, like the one that existed between
Salinas de Gortari and Ernesto Zedillo in 1994. Except that **there are no
parallels, no analogous times, circumstances, or figures**.

In the first place, at present there is no economic crisis as devastating as
the one that broke out in December 1994, which threw millions into poverty,
stripped just as many of their assets, and indebted the country through
Fobaproa to bail out bankers, businessmen and politicians. There isn't even a
crisis.

Zedillo broke with Salinas de Gortari for having handed him Mexico's economy
held together by pins, and then he pulled the pins out, as the other
irresponsible one shot back, in a diatribe that devastated the Nation and
threw them both into the dustbin of history. Let it not be forgotten that the
unheard-of corruption of Raúl Salinas also set them against each other.

In the second place, **Sheinbaum triumphed with 60 percent of the electorate**
, which contrasts with the fraudulent condition of Salinas and of Zedillo
himself. If the former began with spectacular actions, it was because of his
spurious condition, and the latter opened himself to an Electoral Reform
precisely because of the inequity of his election and the damage he did to
Mexico's economy.

Why would Sheinbaum distance herself from or break with López Obrador if both
enjoy, together and separately, a popular support that Salinas and Zedillo
never had, not even Vicente Fox, and much less Felipe Calderón and Enrique
Peña Nieto? What does the President of Mexico gain by separating herself from
her predecessor? Nothing.

The nostalgics of PRI authoritarianism, those who drink from the salinismo
that came to power through crimes and wielded it like a monarch—it even gave
away governorships to the PAN and corrupted intellectuals—see one swallow and
conclude that it is summer. Suddenly, the foul-mouthed Rocha Moya feels like
returning to the governorship of Sinaloa, and this is the evidence that
Sheinbaum has no power and that the one in charge is López Obrador.

Proof? Not a single one. Only the word of the analysts, of course, who belong
to the dirty little school of "the truth is now irrelevant."

The salinismo analysts also claim that today there is no Secretariat of
Governance like when "don Fernando" was there, the torturer and murderer
Gutiérrez Barrios; there is no "iron fist" like with Calderón and the drug
trafficker Genaro García Luna, with whom those analysts frolicked; there is no
"political craft" like with Peña Nieto's PRI, which was very corrupt but
handed out "cuddles," and they even miss the flabby Santiago Creel and his
coordinator of advisers, María Amparo Casar, who became a millionaire by ill
means.

From her presidential candidacy to the first third of her Government, whose
Second Report she presents this Tuesday, September 1, misogynist prianismo has
wanted to "size up" Sheinbaum, and they have been getting surprises.

Sheinbaum has had to set aside figures who, promoted by López Obrador, became
dysfunctional for her six-year project: Adán Augusto López Hernández was
pushed to step down from the coordination of Morena in the Senate over the La
Barredora scandal, and Prosecutor Alejandro Gertz Manero left the post to go
off as Ambassador.

The big fight between Luisa Alcalde and López Beltrán in Morena's national
leadership, which put at risk President Sheinbaum's midterm election, also
entailed the replacement of both, in the logic of electoral effectiveness, not
of a rupture with López Obrador.

And in the months ahead there will surely be more moves in the presidential
Cabinet, also in the logic of effectiveness as a Government in the second
three-year period and to prepare the succession with sufficient room for
maneuver, amid the many forces and groups with legitimate and spurious
interests that the Fourth Transformation is.

Morena's coalition with the Green and Labor parties also entails an intense
negotiation for the distribution of power—that is democracy—but there is no
rationality between having these objectives and breaking with López Obrador,
in what would be devastating for both, above all because of how much history
matters to them.

Why would López Obrador want to stain his legacy with cross-term ambitions and
undue influence over Sheinbaum? Why would he want to imitate Plutarco Elías
Calles? To impose his son on the Presidency of the Republic? He isn't even
Morena's Secretary of Organization anymore. And even if he wanted to promote
him, charisma is not inherited, nor are Mexicans anyone's subjects.

In reality, the salinismo analysts who invoke a Sheinbaum-López Obrador
rupture, those who yearn for it without any rational basis, are the ones who
calculate politically that only a fight could give them an opportunity to
obtain what they have not been able to achieve on their own, neither with
Xóchitl Gálvez nor now with Ricardo Salinas Pliego, a spawn of salinismo.

Finally, the reasoning and the bet of salinismo is not so stupid: a rupture
between Sheinbaum and López Obrador would devastate the movement that both
founded and that has already triumphed twice in overwhelming fashion. Both
know the immense historical cost, and that is, precisely, **what makes it
unviable** …
